item.title: Image issues
item.content:encoded:
On the one hand: I've traced this image back to https://www.freeimages.com/photo/sleepy-head-1-1434634 - Tineye found it on SXC.hu in 2008, and SXC now redirects to FreeImages - it's a stock photo, free for personal and commercial use.

On the other hand: the photographer says "If you'd like to use my photos for your site/project, please let me know where it can be seen (don't forget the image number!)… If the image is of a child who doesn't have a model release, BE SURE TO CLEAR IMAGE USE with me first to be on the safe side (most parents have ok'd for non-profit / educational use only) … Thank you!!! And pretty please: give credit!"

I am fairly certain that she would not be okay with our use of this photo in this context ("it's a super-powered child who gets euthanized in his sleep").

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Very well done. This one of the few SCPs that actually made me sad. At first it seemed like a copy of SCP-239, but it was sufficiently differentiated. It actually reminds me more of the Reality-Bending Cat, who's number I'm too lazy to look up, in that he is mentally incapable of using his abilities for anything more than making himself feel more comfortable.

XK-class scenarios aside, wouldn't it be nice to see SCP-239 and SCP-818 become friends? Why can't the Foundation prioritize romantic happy endings over the preservation of life as we know it?

Anyway, good job taking an almost cliché premise and turning it into a moving and intriguing piece that reminds us of the Foundation's less "heartwarming" side.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I usually dislike reality benders (and kids, for that matter) but this one got me like no other article I've read. It had believability, such as it is, depth of detail without saturation, the profound creepiness of one person being turned into another simply because the subject missed the person they weren't…small, unexpected sadness…and then a genuine chill, like overhearing an ER doc pronounce time of death on someone you've never seen. Wow.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: To me, this… takes the "massively overpowered" vibe and twists it into something quite amazing, not to mention downright tragic. The title has played an important part for me - after reading this, I suddenly realised "abandoned project" could actually refer to the Foundation's work on 818. On one hand I cannot help but wonder what kind of things this boy could do that drove Overwatch to having him killed, on the other someone saying "screw it, we're not wasting any more resources on this thing - finish it off" at some point has really disturbed me.

Not a thrilling one, but definitely one of the best reality bender attempts I've read here. The semi-meta nod to writing these kind of stories is clever, too.

Plus, I kind of feel bad for 818. When human reality benders can use their powers unhampered, it's not that interesting and doesn't really bring out an emotional response. This story shows just how pitiable they can be if the idea is executed properly. I never really cared for 239, but this isn't half bad.
